teams.heading: Jake White drafts ex-England international Nathan Hughes into Fiji's Nations squad
teams.body: Former England international Nathan Hughes returns to the Fiji fold after being drafted into Jake White's 35-man extended squad for the Nations Championship. Hughes, now at Racing 92, last played for England in the 38-38 Six Nations draw with Scotland in 2019. He is one of four uncapped players in the group, alongside Peniami Narisia, Marika Parker and Setareki Bituniyata, all of whom could make their Test debuts this month. Fiji, who beat Japan 34-28 last weekend, begin against France.

lead.why: Fresh squad news naming a player and the uncapped group, and it has not run on this tab before.

teams.heading: Gabe Oghre and Jamie Blamire boost England hooking options amid Tuipulotu concern
teams.body: Gabe Oghre and Jamie Blamire both made strong cases in Leicester's 22-16 PREM win at Bristol Bears on Friday, Planet Rugby's winners-and-losers verdict reads, with the pair's set-piece work framed as a final audition. The spotlight follows an injury concern to Kepu Tuipulotu ahead of the Nations Championship, and the verdict expects both to make the training squad next week. Blamire also got himself on the scoreboard at a crucial period in the contest.

lead.why: England hopefuls' club-match auditions ahead of the Nations Championship, tied to a Tuipulotu injury concern, are the most England-relevant new item in the pack that is not already covered.

teams.body: No matchday squad for France's Test against South Africa has been reported, and today's coverage carries no update on the injury setbacks. teams.heading: Jamie Benson says Farrell called him into Ireland camp before Ulster move
teams.body: Jamie Benson, the 24-year-old Ulster back now in Andy Farrell's Nations Championship squad, says Farrell called him into training in July, before he had linked up with the province. "Obviously, it was a bit of a shock to be called in here before I'd even set foot in Ulster, but it was a great feeling," he said. Benson, who came through Richmond and had been in an England A squad, says his Belfast-raised mother was careful not to push him towards Ireland.

teams.heading: Italy U18 come from behind to beat Ireland 36-29 at Badia Polesine
teams.body: Italy U18 came back from 17-12 down at half-time to beat Ireland 36-29 at Badia Polesine on Saturday, a repeat of last year's win over them in Cosenza. Captain Mesaglio scored Italy's first try, and Fanzo and Agressi both crossed after Ireland had led 22-12 early in the second half, Agressi's try giving the Azzurrini a 26-22 lead. Nikitakos's second yellow card came in the first half, just before Ireland's try that stretched their lead.

lead.why: It is the only genuinely new item in the pack, a result from Saturday, and it is a men's Italy story that the other candidates do not match.

teams.heading: Fergus Watson scores opening try as Glasgow beat Lions 28-20 at Scotstoun
teams.body: Fergus Watson scored the opening try and was named Player of the Match in Glasgow Warriors' 28-20 URC win over the Lions at Scotstoun. He collected a stunning cross kick from Dan Lancaster and skinned Chris Smith on the way over. Glasgow led 19-3 at half-time, with Lancaster also crossing before the break. Morne van den Berg's second-half try brought the Lions within seven, but Glasgow held on.

lead.why: A fresh URC match report with a named Scotland-qualified prospect's standout try, rather than the Singleton debut or Russell interview already covered on this tab.

teams.heading: Carwyn Leggatt-Jones and Ioan Nicholas catch eye in Scarlets' Pretoria defeat
teams.body: The Scarlets were beaten 54-26 by the Bulls in Pretoria after threatening a shock before falling away late on, but WalesOnline's ratings argue the display shows why Wales coaches are watching. Fly-half Carwyn Leggatt-Jones was rated a seven for "Another assured performance by the young fly-half", while Ioan Nicholas also earned a seven, having once again beaten defenders for fun.

teams.heading: Facundo Isa recalled to Argentina squad for Ireland, replacing injured Santiago Grondona
teams.body: Facundo Isa is back in the Argentina squad for the Ireland test, called up in place of the injured Santiago Grondona. The veteran has missed out on international duty in 2024 and 2026, and last played for Argentina in July 2025. Contepomi's 33-man group heads to Dublin with Santiago Grondona, Ignacio Ruiz and Joaquín Oviedo all unavailable, and Oviedo, Gallo and Carreras out long term.

lead.why: Isa's recall is a new squad change, separate from the Gallo and Carreras withdrawals already reported, and it is the most concrete new selection item in the pack.

teams.heading: Harry McLaughlin-Phillips scores and creates as Australia A thump USA 52-0
teams.body: Harry McLaughlin-Phillips, the Bledisloe Cup debutant, scored a try and set up at least three more as Australia A beat the USA Eagles 52-0 in New Jersey, completing a clean sweep of the USA after the opening win in Nashville. McLaughlin-Phillips finished with 17 points, and the forward trio of Nick Frost, Will Harris and Toby Macpherson stole four USA lineouts in the first half. Western Force winger Mac Grealy, whom Les Kiss name-dropped over the weekend, was among several backs with five-pointers.

lead.why: It is the freshest men's story in the pack that is not already in the reader's feed, and it names Wallabies hopefuls performing on tour.

teams.body: Japan have won three and lost two in their last five games, with the sequence running L W W W L, most recent first. teams.heading: Leicester Fainga'anuku's hybrid role gives Rennie bench options, Stephen Donald says
teams.body: Stephen Donald believes Leicester Fainga'anuku, named in the All Blacks squad for the November matches after missing the July games, gives Dave Rennie real bench flexibility. The 27-year-old has mostly played centre or wing but started several games at openside flanker in Super Rugby Pacific this year. A starting spot might be a stretch, but Donald argues: "what doesn't Leicester cover?" It is expected Fainga'anuku will feature in the first northern Test.

teams.heading: Wilco Louw, Ntuthuko Mchunu power Stormers' scrum in 33-7 win over Ulster
teams.body: Wilco Louw and Ntuthuko Mchunu were the platform as the Stormers beat Ulster 33-7 at DHL Stadium on Saturday. The Springbok props regularly sent Ulster's scrum into reverse, and the home pack's maul superiority carried the Cape Town side up the field, leading to a yellow card for visiting prop Keynan Knox. The Stormers were wasteful in the opening half-hour, but the set-piece gave them control. Both props have been named in Rassie Erasmus' Nations Championship squad.

lead.why: A fresh South Africa angle from Saturday's Stormers win: two Springbok props dominated the scrum, and both are named in the Nations Championship squad.
